errors.text: The proposed SPS-plus-HPT treatment does not reconstruct the 6 GPa, 1473 K, 2 h hexahedron-anvil HPHT intervention.
The alloy is identified as AlCoCrFeNi2.1 rather than the target Al0.7CoCrFeNi, and the starting condition is changed from a homogenized bulk alloy to an as-cast or gas-atomized powder route.
The proposed 200 MPa pressure is thirty times below the target 6 GPa pressure and is not representative of the extreme-pressure regime under investigation.
The proposed 1300–1400 degrees Celsius window is substantially hotter than the target 1473 K treatment and lacks evidence for preserving the required phases or patterned structure.
The mechanism omits coherent FCC/B2 interfaces, preferential dislocation transfer, converging phase-specific GND densities, and activation of stacking faults, microbands, and twins.

The HIP comparison is multiply confounded because it removes both SPS and torsional deformation, so it cannot isolate pressure from severe shear deformation, powder consolidation, or processing history.
The stated falsification logic is reversed: failure of low-pressure HIP to reproduce the result would support, not falsify, the claim that the proposed high-intensity treatment is necessary.
The principal SPS/HPT evidence concerns the chemically and mechanically distinct refractory HfNbTaTiZr alloy, and even reports cracking and disputable HPT results.
The cited AlCoCrFeNi2.1 evidence describes the as-cast alloy as having high ductility, contradicting the proposed brittle baseline.
